name: Escalator Cleaner
definition: A purpose-built commercial machine documented to clean escalator or moving-walkway treads, grooves, risers or a defined combination using dry brushing, controlled solution application, suction recovery or step-by-step movement.
excludedScope: Ordinary floor scrubber-dryers without escalator approval
Intervention in escalator controls without site authorization
headline: Escalator cleaner types, tread and riser systems, fit and buyer verification
description: This technical profile distinguishes tread, riser, dry, wet, stationary and step-progressing escalator cleaners and explains moisture, comb, brush, positioning and site-safety checks.
metaDescription: Escalator cleaner guide covering tread and riser systems, wet and dry methods, representative models and procurement checks.
disclaimer: This is an independent category reference, not escalator operation, lockout, maintenance, electrical-safety or cleaning-chemical advice. Obtain the conveyance owner and competent maintenance provider's written procedure for the exact escalator, machine, direction, position, brushes, combs, solution and supervision.

keyFacts.label: Cleaning boundary
keyFacts.value: Treads, grooves, risers and handrails are separate tasks
keyFacts.evidence: Eureka distinguishes EC52 tread cleaning from ERC45 riser cleaning; official sources describe model-specific scope.

keyFacts.label: Operating boundary
keyFacts.value: Machines can be stationary on a moving conveyance or progress step-by-step
keyFacts.evidence: Kärcher describes operation at the lower landing while Columbus describes Step 110 climbing the steps during cleaning.

keyFacts.label: Moisture boundary
keyFacts.value: Solution delivery and recovery must be controlled to protect the conveyance and users
keyFacts.evidence: Kärcher, Columbus and Eureka document simultaneous or controlled wet cleaning and recovery features.
keyFacts.scope: Exact detergent, recovery system, escalator and procedure.

keyFacts.label: Safety boundary
keyFacts.value: Cleaning-machine suitability does not replace escalator operating and maintenance requirements
keyFacts.evidence: ASME A17.1/CSA B44 covers escalator operation and maintenance in North America; machine manuals require trained use.
keyFacts.scope: Applicable jurisdiction, owner procedure and exact conveyance.

systemFlow.name: Site isolation and setup
systemFlow.componentFamily: Barriers, landing position and owner procedure
systemFlow.role: Controls public access and defines authorized conveyance state and direction.
systemFlow.evidence: Standards and manuals place operation within trained, controlled procedures.

systemFlow.name: Machine-to-step interface
systemFlow.componentFamily: Guides, combs, rollers or positioning mechanism
systemFlow.role: Aligns the cleaning head with grooves, tread or riser.
systemFlow.evidence: Kärcher documents guide comb sets; Columbus and Eureka describe model-specific positioning.
systemFlow.scope: Exact step geometry and machine setup.

systemFlow.name: Soil removal
systemFlow.role: Loosens dry debris or bonded soil from the defined surface.
systemFlow.evidence: Official product pages publish brush systems and speeds for named machines.
systemFlow.scope: Brush material, pressure and surface are model-specific.

systemFlow.name: Solution control
systemFlow.componentFamily: Tank, pump, nozzles and approved detergent
systemFlow.role: Applies controlled moisture where wet cleaning is approved.
systemFlow.evidence: Kärcher, Columbus and Eureka describe solution delivery and approved wet cycles.
systemFlow.scope: Exact chemical, dilution, flow and escalator approval.

systemFlow.name: Recovery and handover
systemFlow.componentFamily: Pickup brushes, suction path, recovery tank and dryness check
systemFlow.role: Removes dirty solution and supports safe return to service.
systemFlow.evidence: Official sources document suction and recovery systems.
systemFlow.scope: Achieved dryness and handover remain site-specific.

variants.name: Stationary wet tread cleaner
variants.taskScale: Maintenance or deep cleaning of treads while the conveyance moves under controlled procedure
variants.operatorRelationship: Machine remains positioned at the landing and requires supervision
variants.spaceConstraints: Landing clearance, direction and barrier area are required
variants.limitations: Comb or guide fit and moisture recovery must be approved for the exact escalator.
variants.evidence: Kärcher documents BR 47/35 Esc operation at the lower landing during conveyance movement.

variants.name: Step-progressing wet cleaner
variants.taskScale: Deep cleaning of treads and risers during step-by-step machine travel
variants.operatorRelationship: Trained operator supervises programmed or controlled progression
variants.spaceConstraints: Machine mass, transport and step geometry affect use
variants.limitations: No universal fit or return-to-service time is inferred.
variants.evidence: Columbus describes Step 110 climbing step-by-step and cleaning treads and risers.
variants.scope: Named machine and compatible step geometry.

variants.name: Dry tread or riser-specific cleaner
variants.taskScale: Routine debris removal or dedicated vertical-riser cleaning
variants.operatorRelationship: Machine is positioned or moved according to the defined surface
variants.spaceConstraints: Auxiliary vacuum, trolley or battery logistics can be required
variants.limitations: A riser cleaner does not replace tread cleaning, and dry cleaning may not remove bonded soil.
variants.evidence: Truvox documents dry brushing and vacuum pickup; Eureka distinguishes EC52 treads from ERC45 risers.

performanceMetrics.name: Cleaning scope
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Defines tread, groove, riser or moving-walkway coverage
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Accessory tools and secondary functions must be separated from the main cycle
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Do not compare machines as equivalent if they clean different surfaces.

performanceMetrics.name: Working width and step geometry
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Supports fit to step width, groove and riser dimensions
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Nominal width does not prove comb, guide or edge fit
performanceMetrics.evidence: Kärcher and Columbus publish widths and adjustment features.
performanceMetrics.scope: Actual escalator make, model and step.

performanceMetrics.name: Solution and recovery capacity
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Supports wet-cycle duration and disposal planning
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Tank litres do not establish moisture left in the conveyance
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Recovery result must be verified on site.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Manufacturers publish fresh and recovery tank capacities.

performanceMetrics.name: Brush speed, pressure and material
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Different brush geometries and test conditions prevent simple ranking
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Aggressiveness can damage finishes or increase wear.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official sources publish selected brush data and kits.

performanceMetrics.name: Cleaning time or productivity
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Soil, escalator length, width, method and setup change time
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Manufacturer theoretical or example rates are not achieved site output.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Kärcher and Eureka state method-dependent rates or time boundaries.

applicationFit.evidence: Truvox Cimex X46 integrates vacuum pickup and dry scrubbing; Eureka EC52 includes a dry cycle.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Dry cycles can reduce loose debris before wet work but do not replace deep cleaning of bonded soil.
applicationFit.limitations: No universal cleaning interval is established.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Trial the route and record groove pickup, edge coverage and dust disposal.

applicationFit.application: Wet deep cleaning of escalator treads
applicationFit.evidence: Kärcher, Columbus and Eureka publish dedicated wet-cleaning systems with recovery.
applicationFit.scope: Exact escalator, chemical and machine setup.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Residual moisture and leakage risk should be acceptance criteria, not assumed from tank size.
applicationFit.limitations: No site dryness result is provided.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Require a witnessed demonstration and inspect steps, comb plate, pit and return side before handover.

applicationFit.evidence: Eureka ERC45 is dedicated to washing and vacuum drying vertical step risers; Columbus Step 110 also documents simultaneous tread and riser cleaning.
applicationFit.scope: Named methods and approved step geometry.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Riser coverage should be specified separately from tread claims.
applicationFit.limitations: Handrails and landing plates are not automatically included.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Define every surface in the acceptance checklist and inspect it after the trial.

applicationFit.evidence: Kärcher, Columbus and Eureka publish moving-walkway or travelator compatibility for selected models.
applicationFit.scope: Exact belt or pallet geometry and manufacturer authorization.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: A travelator label does not prove fit to every moving walkway.
applicationFit.limitations: Slope, groove and landing configurations vary.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Obtain written fit confirmation and demonstrate the exact walkway before purchase.

componentStack.name: Guides, combs and positioning hardware
componentStack.role: Align and stabilize the machine at the tread or riser interface.
componentStack.evidence: Official sources document model-specific alignment systems.

componentStack.name: Brush systems
componentStack.role: Loosen debris and bonded soil from grooves, treads or risers.
componentStack.evidence: Manufacturers publish named brush systems and kits.

componentStack.name: Solution system
componentStack.role: Meters approved detergent solution onto the cleaning interface.
componentStack.evidence: Official sources document wet cycles and solution control.

componentStack.name: Recovery and vacuum path
componentStack.role: Collects loosened soil and dirty solution.
componentStack.evidence: Manufacturers publish suction and recovery architectures.

componentStack.name: Power, transport and site controls
componentStack.role: Supplies energy, moves the machine and supports controlled public-area work.
componentStack.evidence: Official pages and manuals publish power, mass and trained-use boundaries.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Exact step fit, authorized conveyance state, solution control and achieved recovery
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Buying by tank size or a universal-fit claim alone
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official sources require model-specific guides, positioning and recovery systems.
procurementDecisions.scope: Exact escalator make, model, step geometry and owner procedure.
procurementDecisions.assessment: A witnessed on-site trial should be mandatory.
procurementDecisions.limitations: No category-wide fit or dryness is established.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Require owner and maintenance-provider approval before the demonstration.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Inspect combs, guides, brush contact, leakage, recovery and the pit after the cycle.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Groove pickup, edge coverage, dust containment and closure time
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Assuming dry brushing removes bonded oils or spills
procurementDecisions.evidence: Truvox and Eureka separate dry debris removal from wet cleaning.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Dry cleaning can form one layer of a multi-method program.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Trial measured dry debris and define when wet or manual detail work is triggered.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Verify brush code, vacuum filter, bag and edge sequence.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Separate coverage of horizontal tread, grooves, vertical riser, edges and landing plates
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Treating a tread cleaner as a complete escalator solution
procurementDecisions.evidence: Eureka explicitly separates EC52 tread and ERC45 riser functions.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Acceptance criteria should list surfaces rather than one overall cleanliness score.
procurementDecisions.limitations: Handrails and pits remain separate unless documented.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Create a surface-by-surface scope and inspect each after the trial.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Confirm which machine or accessory addresses every surface.

engineeringChecks.check: Escalator make, model and step geometry
engineeringChecks.reason: Guide, comb, width and movement interfaces must fit the exact conveyance.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Obtain written compatibility and demonstrate on the target escalator.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Manufacturers describe model-specific adjustment and fit systems.

engineeringChecks.check: Authorized state, direction and landing position
engineeringChecks.reason: Stationary and step-progressing cleaners use different conveyance procedures.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Use an owner-approved written method with trained operators and barriers.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official manuals and ASME safety scope establish controlled operation and maintenance boundaries.

engineeringChecks.reason: Leakage or incompatible chemistry can affect machinery, corrosion and slip risk.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Approve detergent, dilution, flow, recovery and final dryness checks.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official sources publish controlled solution and recovery systems.

engineeringChecks.reason: Machine mass, stairs, cable, battery and brush replacement affect safe deployment.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Plan trolley or lift access, power, storage and replacement parts.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Manufacturers publish mass, electrical and maintenance features.

standards.name: IEC 60335-2-72:2021
standards.applicability: Safety of powered commercial floor-treatment machines within the standard's defined applications and exclusions.
standards.evidence: IEC publishes the scope for commercial sweeping, scrubbing and pickup machines.
standards.scope: Confirm exact machine classification, regional adoption and product conformity; it is not escalator compatibility approval.

standards.name: ASME A17.1/CSA B44
standards.jurisdiction: United States and Canada where adopted
standards.applicability: Safety code covering design, operation, inspection, testing, maintenance, alteration and repair of elevators, escalators and related conveyances.
standards.scope: Conveyance safety baseline; not a cleaning-machine certification or universal operating procedure.

developments.title: IEC commercial floor-treatment safety edition published

developments.scope: International base standard; exact escalator-cleaner classification requires confirmation.

developments.evidence: ASME publishes the catalogue entry and code scope.
